terrain-topdown-atlas.png.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent terrain brush-stamp sprite atlas for a Chinese ink-wash top-down map puzzle. Exact square 4 by 4 equal-cell grid, 16 isolated motifs, generous transparent margins of at least 15 percent inside every cell, no overlap. STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC OVERHEAD PLAN VIEW, looking vertically down at the ground, all objects orientation-independent so stamps may rotate freely. NO horizon, NO front-facing mountains, NO triangular mountain silhouettes, NO isometric view, NO directional cast shadows. Traditional shan shui brushwork translated into cartography: branching ridge crests and pale elevated plateaus seen from directly above, irregular concentric dry-brush contours and fine cun texture, muted malachite grey-green and blue-grey mineral pigments, soft feathered ink edges dissolving into REAL transparent alpha. First row: four small asymmetric rocky hill clusters, rounded and branching in overhead plan. Second row: four long sinuous narrow mountain ridges, different C, S, fork and crescent shapes, interior light summit crests surrounded by darker hachures, visibly seen from above. Third row: two dark dense rugged overhead ridge groups for impassable terrain, then a sparse woodland canopy patch seen straight down as tiny irregular foliage dots, then another overhead woodland cluster. Fourth row: two pale irregular sandy/gravel shoals seen straight down, a tiny scattered overhead reed-and-moss patch, and another small overhead rock patch. Fine authentic ink painting, elegant, limited colors. Terrain stamps only, no rivers, no roads, no hexagon, no tile background, no paper backing, no lettering, no numbers, no grid lines, no labels, no borders, no UI, no symbols. Keep every motif wholly within its own equally sized grid cell. Actual transparent background including around loose brush tips.

scroll-topdown-map.png.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production full-screen background for the Chinese ink-wash hex puzzle 阡陌交通. Wide horizontal handscroll composition, ratio about 16:9. The physical scroll and scholar table are viewed vertically from directly overhead. Two slim vertical dark wooden scroll rollers at the extreme left and extreme right, dark charcoal green antique scholar tabletop visible in a narrow band above and below, thin refined aged silk border, luminous pale warm ivory xuan paper. Inside the scroll is a STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC OVERHEAD Chinese painted topographic map, an elegant ancient shan-chuan yu-tu, not a front-facing landscape. Use tiny branching mountain ridge crests, pale hachured slopes, overhead circular woodland canopies, sinuous narrow waterways and gravel shoals seen straight down, translucent malachite grey-green and pale blue-grey washes, exquisite fine dry-brush ink textures, small drifting mist washes. NO horizon, NO scenic side-view cliffs, NO front-facing mountain silhouettes, NO bamboo stems standing upright, NO isometric mountains, NO cast shadows on terrain. Map details stay at the extreme left and right margins and in the bottom 12 percent of the paper, very pale and airy, fading to blank paper toward the center. Reserve the entire center 65 percent as near-empty light paper for a large game board; also keep the upper-left title area and upper-right score area and middle-left reserve-tile area clean light paper. Avoid any large dark painted masses. The artwork should read as a beautiful subtly painted overhead terrain map on a real horizontal Chinese handscroll. No text at all, no glyphs, no labels, no stamps, no UI, no hexagons, no board, no pieces, no frame around the center. Authentic flat watercolor and ink illustration; physical wooden rollers are the only dimensional objects.
